Cross-Validate an Ordinary GLM Reference Model

Source: R/cv_comparison.R
cross_validate_glm.Rd

Fit a GLM to the analysis rows of each fold and score its predictions for the held-out rows. No scales of effect are estimated. Use this function to build null and nonspatial reference models on the same folds you give cross_validate(), so that a scale-of-effect model has a baseline to beat.

Usage

cross_validate_glm(
  formula,
  data,
  folds,
  family = c("gaussian", "poisson", "binomial", "nbinom2", "Gamma"),
  weights = NULL,
  glm_control = stats::glm.control(),
  metrics = NULL,
  keep_fits = FALSE,
  keep_selection = FALSE,
  theta = NULL,
  dispersion = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

Two-sided model formula, written as for stats::glm(). The response must be a column of data, optionally wrapped in I(), or cbind(successes, failures) for grouped binomial data. Predictors can include factors, interactions, offsets, and the data-dependent terms scale(), poly(), splines::ns(), and splines::bs(). Use y ~ 1 for a null model. Every variable must be a column of data.

data

Data frame with one row per observation, holding the raw responses and every predictor. Its row names are the row IDs that the folds refer to, and they must be unique. Do not supply predictors standardized or transformed with all rows (see "What each fold fits").

folds

Named list of explicit splits, for example from grouped_cv_folds() or spatial_cv_folds(). Each split is a list of two character vectors of row IDs, analysis and assessment, which must not overlap. A row can be left out of a split entirely (for example, by a spatial buffer) and can be assessed in more than one split. Keep rows that share a site, animal, or other sampling unit on the same side of every split.

family

Character response family. Choose "gaussian" (identity link, the default), "poisson" (log), "binomial" (logit), "nbinom2" (negative binomial, log), or "Gamma" (log). Lowercase "gamma" is accepted. For "nbinom2" the variance is mu + mu^2 / theta, where mu is the expected count and theta the size parameter, so a small theta means strong extra variation. For "Gamma" the variance is dispersion x mu^2. Other links and quasi-likelihood families are not supported.

weights

Optional case frequencies, one nonnegative whole number per row of data in the same order. If the vector has names, they must equal the row names. A weight of 3 counts the row three times. A weight of 0 keeps the row in the records but out of the fit and the scores. The default NULL gives every row a weight of one. Gaussian models accept only weights of one. For binomial data, put the trial counts in a cbind(successes, failures) response, not in weights. Weighted proportions are rejected. Some scale-fitting backends add their own weight requirements.

glm_control

Named list of stats::glm.control() settings for the GLM fitted in each fold. The default keeps the settings of glm().

metrics

Optional character vector of scores to record. The defaults depend on family. They are c("rmse", "mae") for Gaussian, c("rmse", "mae", "neg_log_score", "deviance") for Poisson, c("neg_log_score", "brier") for binomial, and c("rmse", "mae", "neg_log_score") for NB2 and Gamma. You can request a subset of the defaults, but not other scores. NB2 and Gamma leave out the deviance because its value depends on theta or the dispersion, which makes it unsuitable for comparing models. Lower is better for every score, and the multiScaleR_cv page defines each one.

keep_fits

Logical. The default FALSE keeps the predictions, scores, fold estimates, and compact diagnostics. TRUE also keeps the full fitted model of every fold in fits, which can use much more memory. You need full fits only to inspect the fold models or to have select_cv() return the selected fits.

keep_selection

Logical. TRUE keeps a compact record of each fold's training likelihood and parameter count in selection_records, which is what select_cv() needs when keep_fits = FALSE. The records come from the fits already run, so they add no fitting time. The default is FALSE.

theta

Optional NB2 size parameter fixed in advance, one positive number. The default NULL estimates theta in each fold with MASS::glm.nb(). A fixed theta is fitted with glm(family = MASS::negative.binomial(theta)) and adds no parameter to K. Fix it only from information independent of the assessment outcomes. Other families reject it.

dispersion

Optional Gamma dispersion fixed in advance, one positive number. The default NULL estimates it in each fold as the training deviance divided by the sum of the frequency weights, the value native Gamma AIC uses. A fixed dispersion adds no parameter to K and is built into the Gamma density before fitting. Fix it only from information independent of the assessment outcomes. Other families reject it.

Value

A list of class multiScaleR_cv, with class multiScaleR_distribution_cv added for "nbinom2" and "Gamma". It has the elements of a cross_validate() result, with these differences. settings$backend is "glm". training holds only the coefficients of each fold, plus the frozen nuisance parameter for NB2 and Gamma. diagnostics holds the convergence record of each fold's GLM, and fits holds ordinary glm objects when keep_fits = TRUE. See multiScaleR_cv for every element and how to read each score.

What each fold fits

Each fold fits glm() to its analysis rows with the declared family and frequency weights, then predicts the expected response of the assessment rows. The families, response forms, weights, and scores are those of cross_validate(). Factors, interactions, and offsets use the native GLM machinery. The constants of scale(), poly(), splines::ns(), and splines::bs() come from the analysis rows, even inside expressions and offsets. Any other preprocessing that learns from the data must also happen within the analysis rows of each fold, so do not supply predictors standardized with all rows. The section "Formula terms that learn from the data" in cross_validate() lists the supported terms and their limits. Missing values are never dropped silently, and native warnings and failed folds are kept. When any fold fails, the function gives one warning with the number of failed folds and their first distinct reasons.

Binomial responses

A binomial response can be numeric or logical 0/1 values, a two-level factor (the second level counts as a success), or cbind(successes, failures) for several trials per row. Keep trial counts in the response and case frequencies in weights, because the two are scored differently.

  • The negative log score of a row is the negative log binomial probability of its observed number of successes, given its trials. Rows are averaged with their frequency weights.

  • The Brier score of a row is the squared error of the predicted success probability, averaged over the row's trials. Rows are averaged with weights equal to frequency weight x trials, so the pooled Brier score is a mean per trial. A row with many trials counts more in the Brier score than in the log score.

  • A row with zero trials or zero weight stays in predictions but contributes to neither score.

  • An observed outcome given zero probability produces an infinite log score. It is kept as is, not clipped.

Negative binomial and Gamma responses

"nbinom2" fits MASS::glm.nb() when theta is estimated and glm(family = MASS::negative.binomial(theta)) when it is fixed, so it needs the MASS package. "Gamma" uses a log link. In each fold the nuisance parameter (theta, or the Gamma dispersion) is estimated from the analysis rows, frozen, and used to score the assessment rows. Coefficients and their native standard errors are those of the native fit. A fixed Gamma dispersion is built into a normalized Gamma family before fitting. The section "Negative binomial and Gamma responses" in cross_validate() describes how these parameters enter K and the rules they follow.

How to read the Gamma dispersion

distribution[[fold]]$dispersion is the training deviance divided by the training sum of case frequencies, the value native Gamma AIC uses. It is held fixed when the held-out Gamma densities are scored. Native coefficient standard errors use the Pearson dispersion instead, so they can rest on a different number. The density dispersion does not replace that coefficient uncertainty. convention records the rule that produced the value, and estimated is FALSE when you fixed it with dispersion. Supply theta or dispersion only when the value is known or was fixed independently of the assessment outcomes.

What the scores do and do not include

Predictions use each fold's fitted parameters as if they were known. They do not integrate parameter uncertainty, provide prediction intervals, or establish calibration. Use cross_validate() to estimate scales of effect within the same folds.

See also

cross_validate(), cv_tab(), select_cv(), multiScaleR_cv, and vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

data("landscape_counts")   # counts and a site-level covariate
data("surv_pts")           # survey locations
# Three spatial folds. The simulated coordinates are in meters.
folds <- spatial_cv_folds(crds(vect(surv_pts)), block_size = 1000, k = 3,
                          crs = 32617)

# Null and site-only reference models on the same folds
null_cv <- cross_validate_glm(counts ~ 1, landscape_counts, folds,
                              family = "poisson")
site_cv <- cross_validate_glm(counts ~ site, landscape_counts, folds,
                              family = "poisson")
site_cv   # pooled held-out scores, lower is better
#> Cross-validation: 3 of 3 folds scored; 100 of 100 input rows assessed.
#>         metric estimate        unit n_assessment n_scored weight_sum complete
#>           rmse 2.232857 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#>            mae 1.661678 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#>  neg_log_score 2.169778 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#>       deviance 2.372818 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
cv_tab(list(null = null_cv, site = site_cv), metric = "neg_log_score")
#>   Modnames Rank    Score       Delta        Metric        Unit N_assessment
#> 1     null    1 2.163750 0.000000000 neg_log_score observation          100
#> 2     site    2 2.169778 0.006027989 neg_log_score observation          100
#>   N_scored Weight_sum Warnings
#> 1      100        100        0
#> 2      100        100        0

# Negative binomial: theta is estimated in each fold and frozen for scoring
if (requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)) {
  nb_cv <- cross_validate_glm(counts ~ site, landscape_counts, folds,
                              family = "nbinom2")
  sapply(nb_cv$distribution, function(d) d$theta)   # small theta: overdispersed
}
#>    fold1    fold2    fold3 
#> 1.561918 1.438781 1.939947 

# Gamma model for a strictly positive response
i <- 1:96
positive <- data.frame(
  y = exp(0.2 + 0.35 * sin(i * 0.73)) *
    rep(c(0.3, 0.6, 1.1, 2.4, 0.8, 1.8, 0.4, 1.6), 12),
  x = sin(i * 0.73))
gamma_folds <- grouped_cv_folds(rep(letters[1:12], each = 8), k = 3)
gamma_cv <- cross_validate_glm(y ~ x, positive, gamma_folds, family = "Gamma")
gamma_cv$summary
#>          metric  estimate        unit n_assessment n_scored weight_sum complete
#> 1          rmse 0.9077540 observation           96       96         96     TRUE
#> 2           mae 0.7704337 observation           96       96         96     TRUE
#> 3 neg_log_score 1.1450485 observation           96       96         96     TRUE
# Training deviance / sum of case frequencies, frozen for scoring each fold
sapply(gamma_cv$distribution, function(d) d$dispersion)
#>     fold1     fold2     fold3 
#> 0.4401327 0.4399048 0.4391975
